_comment: The sources of the content, and their licences.
This file is the machine-readable version of the table in
readme.md. It is written by the pipeline (01_fetch_sources.py
keeps the download manifest) and it is what the app shows
The audio licences are per contributor: Tatoeba is CC BY 2.0 FR
as a corpus, but every sentence carries its own licence and
the audio of a sentence is contributed by a person. The
and are copied into the content database with the sentences.

sources.name: CC-CEDICT
sources.used_for: definitions and part of speech for the vocabulary

sources.name: Make Me a Hanzi
sources.used_for: stroke order and radical for the characters

sources.name: HSK 3.0 word lists
sources.used_for: the graded vocabulary and the level of every word

sources.name: Chinese Grammar Wiki (AllSet Learning)
sources.used_for: the grammar points and their example sentences

sources.name: Tatoeba
sources.used_for: the sentence corpus and the human audio
sources.note: The audio is contributed per sentence by individual people. The per-sentence licence is in the license column of sentences_with_audio.csv and travels with the sentence into the content database.

sources.name: pinyin-data
sources.used_for: the per-character readings and the syllable inventory

sources.name: phrase-pinyin-data
sources.used_for: the pinyin of the multi-character words

sources.name: Chinese Wiktionary (via kaikki.org)
sources.used_for: the human Bulgarian glosses and the part of speech

sources.name: NLLB-200
sources.used_for: the machine Bulgarian glosses, grammar and sentences
sources.note: NON-COMMERCIAL. This is the licence that blocks paid distribution: the machine glosses would have to be replaced with human ones or with a model under a permissive licence before any paid release. The column gloss_source says which glosses came from the model.

sources.name: Microsoft Edge TTS (Azure Neural Voices)
sources.license: no licence on the audio itself; the voice is a Microsoft Azure Neural Voice
